## Purpose and runtime shape
NetPulse is a self-hosted LAN network-monitoring and management system for OpenWrt/GL.iNet fleets. Its primary runtime is a Go server that embeds and serves a React PWA, persists state/time series in SQLite, and communicates with routers through read-only SSH polling and optional local agents. Main entry points: `server-go/cmd/netpulse/main.go`, `agent/cmd/netpulse-agent/main.go`, and optional latency sidecar `collector/main.go`.

## Server composition and HTTP boundary
The server bootstraps configuration, persistence, polling, background services, and HTTP/SSE routes. `server-go/internal/httpapi/server.go` is the API assembly boundary; route handlers span monitoring data, management actions, auth, firmware, alerts, and settings in `server-go/internal/httpapi/`. The static SPA is embedded and served through `server-go/internal/staticspa/staticspa.go`. Authentication, roles, and API tokens are isolated in `server-go/internal/auth/auth.go` and `server-go/internal/apitoken/store.go`.

## Router observation and agent ingress
The server discovers and polls network devices, primarily via SSH/OpenWrt commands and adapters. `server-go/internal/poller/poller.go` schedules collection; `server-go/internal/adapters/openwrt.go`, `server-go/internal/adapters/agent.go`, and `server-go/internal/adapters/snmp_live.go` normalize OpenWrt, agent, and SNMP switch observations into server models. Agent-facing HTTP endpoints and state handling live in `server-go/internal/httpapi/agent.go` and `server-go/internal/httpapi/agentstate.go`. SSH key management and pooled access form an external-device boundary at `server-go/internal/sshkey/sshkey.go` and `server-go/internal/adapters/sshpool.go`.

## Edge agent
`netpulse-agent` runs on OpenWrt under procd/init scripts and reports richer local telemetry to the server. Its runtime handles configuration, pairing, firmware operations, and server connectivity in `agent/runtime/runtime.go`, `agent/runtime/pairing.go`, and `agent/runtime/upgrade.go`. Probes collect local, LLDP, memory, and client-bandwidth evidence in `agent/probe/probe.go`, `agent/probe/lldp.go`, and `agent/probe/clientbw.go`. Push/SSE support enables server-directed work and live state via `agent/internal/push/push.go` and `agent/internal/sseclient/sseclient.go`.

## Network model, history, and topology
Normalized observations feed SQLite-backed stores and derived views. Database lifecycle, migrations, and rollups are centralized in `server-go/internal/db/db.go`. Topology derives router/client/switch relationships from FDB and LLDP, with persistent user overrides, in `server-go/internal/adapters/topology.go`, `server-go/internal/adapters/lldp.go`, and `server-go/internal/topooverride/topooverride.go`. Alert rules and suppression evaluate changing conditions in `server-go/internal/alerts/alerts.go`, `server-go/internal/alerts/rules.go`, and `server-go/internal/alerts/suppression.go`.

## Controlled write operations
Monitoring is separated from explicit admin-triggered changes. The HTTP API invokes orchestration modules for services such as DAWN, usteer, SQM, guest Wi-Fi, DDNS, and WireGuard through `server-go/internal/orchestr/orchestr.go` and `server-go/internal/orchestr/modules.go`. Firmware workflows—including scheduling and OpenWrt `owut` flows—are contained in `server-go/internal/firmware/engine.go`, `server-go/internal/firmware/scheduler.go`, and `server-go/internal/firmware/owut.go`. These are the principal mutation boundary versus the polling/adapters path.

## Frontend and real-time delivery
The TypeScript React PWA enters at `app/src/main.tsx` and is composed by `app/src/App.tsx`. `app/src/data/DataProvider.tsx` is the client data boundary, while `app/src/data/AuthContext.tsx` manages authenticated UI state. Fleet, topology, and operational views are represented by `app/src/pages/Routers.tsx`, `app/src/pages/Topology.tsx`, and `app/src/pages/Orchestration.tsx`. Server SSE fan-out is implemented by `server-go/internal/sse/hub.go` and `server-go/internal/sse/agenthub.go`.

## Infrastructure and integrations
Deployment targets Linux/systemd and OpenWrt packages: `deploy/netpulse-go.service`, `deploy/openwrt/netpulse-server/Makefile`, and `deploy/openwrt/netpulse-agent/Makefile`. External/local integrations include OpenWrt ubus/SSH, SNMP switches, AdGuard Home, WireGuard, Proxmox, Web Push, ntfy, and Telegram, represented by `server-go/internal/adapters/adguard.go`, `server-go/internal/adapters/proxmox.go`, `server-go/internal/ntfy/ntfy.go`, and `server-go/internal/telegram/telegram.go`.
